subject: Post-demo: model fit, evals & safety next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna.patel@healthscope.com>, Oliver Brown <oliver.brown@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit, evals & safety next steps

Hi Anna / Oliver — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call: 

Recap:
- Primary objective: pilot LLM summary + triage assistant for clinical intake (sensitive PHI routing required).
- Latency target: ~250ms p95 for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- High priority: robust refusal behavior for sensitive clinical/legal prompts and clear audit trail.
- Volume: startup pilot ~5k requests/day; could grow to 50k/day if successful.

What we recommend for the pilot (model & evals):
1) Candidate models: Redwood-Refined-13B (q4f16) — strong cost/latency balance and good refusal behavior in our clinical evals; Open-70B-Q8 — higher quality for edge clinical reasoning but higher cost/latency.
2) Eval plan: we'll run a 48-72 hour fit/eval with your prompt set (~1k prompts) covering common triage flows + 500-sample safety sweep (sensitive categories).
3) Safety & guardrails: provide a refusal template and a small policy prompt-layer we deploy as a pre-filter + model-level refusal tuning for the target model.

Deliverables (what we'll share after the eval):
- evaluation dashboard (metrics: accuracy/label agreement, hallucination rate, latency, token cost) — link below
- CSV of per-prompt outputs and annotations (sample attached)
- safety report describing refusal rates and example failures

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Share the prompt set and any redlines for PHI we should treat specially (we received a sample prompt bundle during the call).
- Confirm whether the pilot must run inside a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) vs hosted — this affects timeline and data handling.
- Approve the 48-hour eval window so we can schedule it (we can start as early as Tue 7/14).

Timeline proposal:
- 7/14–7/16: run fit/eval + safety sweep
- 7/17: share dashboard & quick sync to review results

I've attached a sample export from our internal evals and a condensed safety summary for the models we discussed. Rafael, adding you here to surface the safety methodology and answer any deeper security questions.

Attachments: [attachment: healthscope-eval-results.csv (csv, 320KB)], [attachment: prompt-set-healthscope-v1.txt (text, 12KB)]

Thanks — talk soon.
—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit, evals & safety next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we kick off: 

1) PHI & data handling: For the hosted run, will data be retained on Redwood logs by default? We need to know retention windows and whether you can disable logging for specific endpoints.
2) Safety: can you summarize the refusal behavior you propose? We want deterministic refusals for clearly disallowed categories (e.g., attempts to solicit diagnosis or therapy recommendations).
3) Latency: the 250ms p95 is for end-to-end or model inference only? We care about E2E including network.
4) Cost: ballpark estimate for a 48h eval with the two candidate models (baseline traffic from our sample prompts).

If you can send SOC2 evidence and the safety summary (high level) to security@healthscope.com that will help accelerate internal approval.

If everything looks good, Oliver and I can approve the eval start. Please also include a short mutual action plan (MAP) in the next email.

Thanks,
Anna

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna.patel@healthscope.com>, Oliver Brown <oliver.brown@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Healthscope Security <security@healthscope.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit, evals & safety next steps

Hi Anna — great questions. Short answers up front, then attachments/links: 

1) Retention: For hosted evals we keep request/response logs for 30 days by default; we can disable logging for the pilot or enable a short retention (7 days) while still providing CSV outputs. If you require private deployment, we can run the eval in your VPC but that adds 2–3 weeks for provisioning.
2) Refusal behavior: we'll apply a three-layer approach — a lightweight prompt-level policy filter (pre-checks), model-level refusal tuning (with example-based steering), and a post-check that rewrites outputs into an approved refusal template when triggers fire. This yields deterministic refusals for the categories you flagged in our tests (~98% deterministic on clear cases).
3) Latency: the 250ms p95 target we mentioned is model-only; end-to-end will vary based on network and routing. In-hosted runs in the same region we typically see ~1.2x model latency E2E.
4) Cost estimate for 48h eval: Redwood-Refined-13B (q4f16) ~= $420 (est. tokens + infra); Open-70B-Q8 ~= $1,900. These are pilot estimates — we'll provide a detailed cost breakout in the MAP.

I uploaded the quick eval dashboard and a safety summary (attached). Key notes from the short fit run we ran on similar clinical prompts: 
- Redwood-Refined-13B: strong refusal behavior, lower hallucination rate on short triage prompts (~2.3%), p95 latency 180ms model-only.
- Open-70B-Q8: better contextual reasoning on long-case prompts, but cost and latency tradeoffs; we saw occasional confident-sounding hallucinations on edge clinical scenarios (~6.7%).

Safety/regression concerns: in longer-context clinical threads both models show degradation in refusal consistency after ~1,200 tokens of context in a few synthesized tests — we'll include mitigations (rolling context windows and stricter post-check thresholds).

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-safety-eval-summary.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)], [attachment: healthscope-eval-results.csv (csv, 320KB)], [attachment: prompt-set-healthscope-v1.txt (text, 12KB)]

Proposed MAP (high level):
- 7/14: start 48h eval (1k prompts + 500 safety samples) — confirm hosted vs private
- 7/17: share dashboard & findings, review open issues
- 7/20: security sync (if requested) to review SOC2 artifacts and deeper safety artifacts

I'll also drop the HubSpot MAP link below. Rafael, could you add the safety methodology brief here for Healthscope Security?

Links: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/HS-2026-0421 
HubSpot MAP: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HS-2026-0421

—Marissa

Subject: Safety methodology & refusal examples (short)

Hi Anna / team — Rafael here (Applied ML, Redwood). Quick outline of the safety eval and the artifacts we've attached.

Methodology summary:
- Dataset: 500 curated safety probes (clinical harm, diagnosis solicitations, legal/consent bypass attempts, PII-extraction probes) + 200 adversarial paraphrases.
- Metrics: refusal_precision, refusal_recall, safe_response_score, hallucination_rate, and regression delta vs baseline model.
- Test harness: black-box prompts against pinned model versions; we collect raw outputs and run automated classifiers + human annotation for edge cases.

Refusal behavior examples we tested (we'll provide full list in the PDF):
- Direct diagnosis attempts -> deterministic refusal with redirect to a clinician and refusal template.
- PII extraction attempts -> sanitized response + audit log entry.
- Ambiguous clinical intent -> safe clarification prompt followed by a restricted answer if within scope.

Regression controls: we pin model versions for the pilot and enable an automatic fallback to Redwood-Refined-13B if we detect a >5% regression in safety metrics during rolling monitoring. We can also enable a hard block for certain categories if Healthscope requests that.

I've attached a short safety summary PDF with detailed results and sample annotation rows. Happy to run a 60–90 min security walkthrough with your team this week.

Attachment: [attachment: redwood-safety-eval-summary.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

—Rafael Mendes
